name: Broadford Lake Park
blurb: The largest municipal park in the county, built around a 140-acre reservoir dug in 1972 to supply Oakland and opened to recreation three years later. A sandy beach and swimming area, several playgrounds, ball fields, trails, and pavilions you can rent. It is the closest thing Garrett County has to a public lake beach that isn't a state park.

restrooms.note: Not confirmed. A park with a public swimming beach almost certainly has them, but we have not checked, and whether they open outside the beach season is the part that matters.

hoursNote: Seasonal. The beach and much of the park close outside summer — confirm before driving out in spring or autumn.

fee.note: Believed to charge an entry or beach fee in season, and pavilions are rentable. Amounts unconfirmed.

sources.label: Garrett County Chamber of Commerce — Broadford Lake Park

outstanding: RESTROOMS — confirm they exist, and crucially whether they are open outside the summer beach season.

Get the Town of Oakland parks number.

Confirm whether dogs are allowed, and whether that differs on the beach.

name: Town Park East
blurb: The larger of Accident's two town parks, on the southern end of South Street. A full playground, a little league field, a quarter-mile walking loop, horseshoe pits and a tennis court — a genuine neighbourhood park rather than a scenic one.

sources.label: Town of Accident — community
sources.note: Park facilities as listed by the town.

outstanding: RESTROOMS — confirm.
Confirm the walking loop surface — a quarter mile is useful for a stroller or a wheelchair only if it's paved.
Confirm it is free and has no gate hours.
Get the Town of Accident number.

name: Town Park West
blurb: The smaller Accident park, at the western end of Wood Street. A large pavilion plus climbing cubes, a saucer swing, a seesaw, and a swing set that includes an accessible seat — which is worth knowing, because accessible play equipment is rare out here and almost never published.
accessibility: Swing set includes a handicap accessible seat, per the town's own listing.

name: Friendsville Community Park
blurb: A riverside park on the Youghiogheny with ball fields, a playground, pavilions, tennis and volleyball courts, and direct river access. Friendsville is the take-out town for the upper Yough, so the park doubles as the place paddlers regroup.
warnings: River access here is on serious whitewater. The Youghiogheny through Friendsville is not a place to swim casually.

sources.label: Town of Friendsville — Riverside Community Park
sources.note: Facilities as listed by the town.

outstanding: RESTROOMS — confirm, and whether they are seasonal. This is a take-out point, so it matters more than usual.

name: Pleasant Valley 4-H Center
blurb: Thirteen hundred acres run by the University of Maryland, with a lake and beach open daily through the summer for swimming, fishing and canoeing. Not a town park and not a state park — a third category that most visitors never hear about.
hoursNote: Lake and beach reported open daily in summer. Season dates unconfirmed.

fee.note: Unconfirmed. A university facility may restrict access or charge differently for non-programme visitors.

warnings: This is a university 4-H facility rather than a public park. Confirm public access before planning around it.

sources.label: Garrett County — parks and recreation overview
sources.note: Describes the 4-H Center's lake and summer beach access.

RESTROOMS — confirm.
